integrity: An analytic Gaussian tilting identity and finite geometric sums prove the claim. The standalone checker tests exact algebra and boundary examples, not an infinite theorem. No external scientific or independent validation has been performed.
scientific_limitations: Exact finite-n mixed covariance and two negative-unit-root asymptotic scales. Existence, not uniqueness, of sign zeros is proved; parameter-critical values require higher-order terms. The 2006 archival paper is a historical context source, not a source for the new theorem. The full Sinn–Keller article was unavailable for historical comparison; independent novelty is not certified.
title: Two boundary layers for zero-crossing and squared-sum covariance in Gaussian AR(1)
